A little story-telling to explain how I first came across this
I was terrified of spiders as a little girl and used to scream for my mom to get
rid of any spiders in my room. We moved to Texas from Holland when I was
12, and I went camping with my Biology teacher and a group in the Big Ben.
There are a LOT of TARANTULAS in that National park and I was terrified.
Now I trusted Mr Hoke, so when he told me he was going to do something to
help me with the fear of spiders and to trust him, I did.
He came and sat next to me and had a tarantula in his hand, while telling me
to look at his face and to tell him what was going through my mind.
I told him I was terrified of spiders, that they are creepy and crawly and my
He told me to take a breath and look at the spider.
I did, and I wasn’t that terrified. I took another breath and continued looking.
I thought, “oh wow, it is big,” and took another breath.
I noticed my heart rate had slowed down and said so.
I said “I am not so afraid anymore.”
I saw the little hairs on the legs of the Tarantula.
My breath was much slower and I felt my shoulders soften.
I looked at my teacher and grinned, “this is not so bad, although it is so much
bigger than the spiders we have in Holland”.
He asked if I wanted to hold it….
The first thought was, “Oh my god, how will it feel?”
The Image was of the spider on my hand.
The emotion that came up was curiousity.
The body sensation was tingling in my fingers.
I became more intrigued by how soft the tarantula felt. (Thought)
I looked at its long legs and round body. (Image)
In a matter of 5 minutes, a fear that had held me hostage for many years lifted.
I couldn’t believe how simple it was!
This is a beautiful practice to be more in the here and now, and, is a great alternative for those
who find guided meditations difficult to follow.
